# ecommerce-creative

Shared Talia skill package. The instruction entrypoint is SKILL.md; this package contains declarative text and supporting reference assets only.

See LICENSE and NOTICE for license and provenance.
files.SKILL.md:
---
name: ecommerce-creative
description_zh: "基于商品事实和原素材编写电商主图文案、图片提示词、视频脚本与分镜，提供跨渠道素材 brief 和测试方向；用于商品创意策划，不负责实际生成媒体或发布广告。"
description_en: "Create ecommerce image copy, product image prompts, video scripts and storyboards grounded in product facts and source assets. Use for cross-channel creative briefs and experiments, not actual media generation or ad publication."
---

# Ecommerce Creative

Turn verified product facts into executable creative briefs. For shared message selection and revision, read `@skill/ecommerce-listing/references/source-based-writing.md` through the available `ecommerce-listing` Skill. Then resolve the placement, source assets, format and requested action for the creative route.

- For image/detail-page copy, read [visual copywriting](references/visual-copywriting.md).
- For generation-ready briefs, read [product visual prompts](references/product-visual-prompts.md).
- For hooks, scripts and shot plans, read [video storyboards](references/video-ad-storyboard.md).
- Apply [claim checks](references/creative-compliance.md) to the selected route; deliver with [output guidance](references/creative-output-templates.md).

Use the approved direction when present. If a material creative decision is unresolved, present a small concrete choice while completing independent work; do not add a mandatory approval stop to every draft. Detailed directions, prompts and storyboards are deliverables, not generated media. Hand actual production to the available media capability with the fact and asset brief; retain its existing general-purpose workflow and permissions.

This Skill requires no paid provider and invokes no generation or publication service itself.
files.references/creative-compliance.md:
# Creative claim checks

Check both visible wording and implied visual outcomes against product evidence. A disclaimer does not prove an exaggerated demonstration. Keep packaging, certifications, accessories, test results, prices and promotion conditions accurate for the displayed variant.

Record asset provenance and permitted use in the production brief. Use market/category/placement-specific official rules only when relevant, with source and verification date; if unavailable, name the unverified constraint. Do not export one country's absolute-word rule to every platform or language.

For a main-image slot, secondary image, content video or paid ad, establish the actual format and overlay requirements. Keep finished copy separate from evidence placeholders. This review establishes brief readiness, not rendered quality, rights clearance for unknown assets, platform approval or publication.
files.references/creative-output-templates.md:
# Creative delivery

Return only requested assets: a message card, complete image copy, generation-ready brief or full storyboard. A storyboard can use: time | SKU/source | visual | exact caption | narration | proof | CTA.

Apply the shared writing method linked from the Skill root to the full storyboard, including captions, narration and implied demonstrations. Creative staging describes a proposed shot, not evidence that the product achieved a result.

When handing off to media production, include the relevant fact/asset brief: resolved product identifiers, approved copy, preservation requirements, supported effects, missing evidence, target placement/specification and acceptance criteria. Proposed shots remain proposed until actual media exists and is inspected.

If alternatives are useful, show a small set that changes the message or execution, not product facts. Include an experiment only when it answers a real uncertainty. Reuse the user's approved direction without another confirmation round.
files.references/product-visual-prompts.md:
# Product visual brief

Bind each asset to product/SKU, color, dimensions, quantity, packaging text, logo, included accessories, source file and permitted edits. State which elements require original-pixel preservation and which background or scene can change. Do not imply source fidelity can be guaranteed by a negative prompt alone.

Specify subject, composition, background, light, palette, aspect ratio and text-safe areas. Supply exact overlay copy separately from illustrative generation. If there is no reliable product reference, label the result as concept direction rather than an accurate product rendering.

For motion specify starting asset, per-shot SKU, camera/subject movement, duration, transitions and captions. Avoid demonstrations whose mechanism, accessory or performance is unsupported by the product facts. A scene must not imply water resistance, load rating or medical benefit merely because it looks persuasive.

Pass the brief to the existing image/video production capability. Its actual-output inspection should establish variant/packaging consistency, text correctness, readable layout and requested file specifications; this brief cannot assert that inspection occurred.
files.references/video-ad-storyboard.md:
# Video creative

Choose the structure for the placement and audience: reason to watch → use or problem → supported product demonstration → objection → action. Before delivering a timed script, run `storyboard_timing` on its final narration and shot windows. Shorten or redistribute over-budget lines, allow for the requested delivery style and visual actions, and rerun after revising text or timing.

TikTok Shop, Douyin, Kuaishou and short-form placements may need hooks and creator-style demonstrations; a storefront product video may need a calm specification/use sequence. Treat these as creative options and validate with the supplied channel data. Do not invent testimonials or pretend a scripted actor's experience is an actual review.

Each shot records time, SKU/source asset, visual action, factual proof, exact caption, narration and CTA. At a variant cut, reset the product, price, quantity and captions together. Keep claimed accessories and effects bound to evidence.

For experiments vary the hook, first frame, proof or CTA separately. Use the platform's actual view/click/conversion definitions and comparable windows. View-through or attributed sales do not by themselves establish incremental lift; returns and complaints can reveal an expectation gap.

## Check script timing

Use the execution template returned when reading this Skill: script name
`storyboard_timing` (without a file extension), arguments `--input timing.json`.
The [script](../scripts/storyboard_timing.js) runs the shared local narration estimator without producing audio or opening
a video-production project.

Prepare working JSON from the script's exact spoken lines and planned shot
times. Each segment has `id`, `text`, `start_sec` and `target_sec` (duration,
not end time). Include silent shots with empty `text`; omit captions and stage
directions from speech. Segments are ordered and do not overlap.

```json
{
  "duration_sec": 15,
  "segments": [
    {"id": "opening", "start_sec": 0, "target_sec": 3, "text": "A fresh start."},
    {"id": "detail", "start_sec": 3, "target_sec": 9, "text": ""},
    {"id": "cta", "start_sec": 12, "target_sec": 3, "text": "Find your favorite."}
  ]
}
```

Optional `speed` is a multiplier from 0.5 to 2, default 1 for a natural-pace
estimate. Use the requested pace when specified; do not raise speed merely to
make crowded copy fit. This is an estimate, not a voice-specific measurement
or a guarantee of relaxed delivery.

Each result reports `estimated_sec` and `remaining_sec` for the exact text
identified by `text_sha256`. Negative remaining time indicates that the line
needs more time under that estimate. `remaining_timeline_sec` compares the last
shot's end with the requested duration; total speech alone does not prove that
each shot fits. Positive remaining time can support a pause or visual action;
judge those against the actual scene and style rather than filling every gap
with more words.

Revise the script and its working JSON together, then rerun for the final text
and timings. The script does not rewrite the deliverable or approve a shoot.
Return the requested storyboard through the normal output tools; the estimate
JSON is working material, not an additional requested deliverable.
files.references/visual-copywriting.md:
# Visual copywriting

Build a message card: audience and scenario, buying objection, supported benefit, factual proof, source asset and intended placement. Prioritize one message per image and make the product/variant recognizable.

Distinguish product-main-image slots, secondary infographics, brand hero images and promotional ads. Their overlay and layout requirements differ; use the actual placement brief or verified current rules. Amazon, Taobao/Tmall, JD, Pinduoduo, Shopify, Shopee and other storefronts do not share one mandatory image sequence or copy allowance.

A useful optional sequence is product identity → benefit → specification → use → objection/offer. Choose the number of images to match the task. Keep text readable at delivery size; Chinese character-count rules do not transfer to another language or aspect ratio. Put dimensions, included quantity and compatibility where they prevent a wrong purchase.

For localized revisions preserve the approved message and unchanged product facts. Do not turn a price edit into a new design direction.
